items.stem: Which is outside evidence, a fact that isn't in this document, that helps explain it?

options.1: Locke writes that the power passes back to the people when a legislature seizes it.
options.2: England had just replaced King James II with William and Mary, on Parliament's own terms.
options.3: Locke was an important thinker whose ideas about government influenced many writers who came after him.
options.4: The Tokugawa shogun closed Japan to most foreign trade in the 1630s, leaving only a small Dutch post at Nagasaki.

hints: One choice is already in the document in front of you.
Two choices are specific and true. Only one of them has anything to do with Locke.
items.rationale: Outside evidence is specific, is not in the document, and connects to it. England's change of king is what Locke was writing about. Japan's closing is specific and true but does not help explain Locke, and calling him an important thinker is too vague to count.

stimulus.title: Document 2 · Locke on a government that breaks the deal
stimulus.content: “[When] the legislature shall . . . grasp [for] themselves, or put into the hands of any other, an absolute power over their lives, liberties, and estates of the people, . . . they forfeit the power the people had put into their hands for quite contrary ends, and it [passes] to the people, who have a right to resume their original liberty. . . .”
stimulus.citation: Source: John Locke, Two Treatises of Government, 1690 (adapted)

items.stem: Which is outside evidence that helps explain this document?

options.1: Montesquieu writes that there can be no liberty when the legislative and executive powers are united.
options.2: Government is complicated, and people have argued about the best way to organize it for centuries.
options.3: The U.S. Constitution of 1787 split power into three branches, as Montesquieu had urged.
options.4: The kingdom of Benin traded pepper, ivory and cloth with Portuguese merchants from the late 1400s.

hints: One choice is in the document already.
Which government put Montesquieu's plan into practice?
items.rationale: The U.S. Constitution is a specific fact from outside the document that shows Montesquieu's idea mattered. Benin is specific and true but unconnected, and saying government is complicated names no person, date or event.

stimulus.title: Document 4 · Montesquieu on powers united in one person
stimulus.content: “When the legislative and executive powers are united in the same person, or in the same body of magistrates [government officials], there can be no liberty; because apprehensions [fears] may arise, lest the same monarch or senate should enact tyrannical laws to execute them in a tyrannical manner. . . .”
stimulus.citation: Source: Baron de Montesquieu, The Spirit of the Laws, 1748 (adapted)

items.stem: Which is outside evidence that helps explain this document?

options.1: Pugachev's Rebellion, from 1773 to 1775, showed how angry Russia's serfs had already become.
options.2: The decree orders that serfs who complain about their landlords be whipped and sent away.
options.3: Russia was a very large country with a great many people living in its countryside.
options.4: Louis XIV built the palace at Versailles and kept France's leading nobles living there with him.

hints: Which choice is not in the document, but tells you what happened next in Russia?
Two choices are specific. Only one of them is about the people in this decree.
items.rationale: Pugachev's Rebellion is specific, from outside the document, and connected to it: it shows what the decree's harshness led to. Versailles is specific and true but about a different ruler, and calling Russia a large country names no person, date or event.

stimulus.title: Document 10 · Catherine's government on serfs
stimulus.content: “The Governing Senate . . . has deemed it necessary to make known that the landlords' serfs and peasants . . . owe their landlords proper submission and absolute obedience in all matters . . . . And should . . . any serfs and peasants . . . make bold to submit unlawful petitions [formal written complaints] complaining of their landlords, and especially to petition Her Imperial Majesty personally, then both those who make the complaints and those who write up the petitions shall be punished by the knout [a heavy whip] and forthwith deported to Nerchinsk to penal servitude [forced labor as punishment] for life . . . . it shall be read in all the churches on Sundays and holy days . . . lest anyone pretend ignorance.”
stimulus.citation: Source: A Source Book for Russian History, G. Vernadsky, trans., Yale University Press, 1972 (adapted)

options.1: It is long, and it fills up most of the space under the question.
options.2: It repeats what the document already says, using new words of your own.
options.3: It is specific, a name, date or event, accurate, and tied to the document.
options.4: It comes from any part of history you happen to remember from an earlier unit.

hints: Outside evidence has to do work, not decorate.
Think name, date, event, and a connection to this document.
items.rationale: Strong outside evidence is specific, accurate, and connected to the document. Length proves nothing, repeating the document is not outside evidence at all, and a fact with no connection does no work.

items.stem: Which is outside evidence that helps explain this document?

options.1: Wollstonecraft writes that men who shut women out of the new rights act like tyrants.
options.2: Women have always been important to history, and writers have been saying so for centuries.
options.3: The Ottoman Empire lost much of its trade when Europeans found new sea routes to Asia.
options.4: France's constitution of 1791 gave the vote to some men and to no women at all.

hints: One choice is in the document. One is specific but has nothing to do with her argument.
Which fact tells you what Wollstonecraft was answering when she wrote?
items.rationale: France's 1791 constitution is the outside fact Wollstonecraft was answering. It is specific, and it is not in her text. The Ottoman choice is true but unconnected, and saying women have always been important names no person, date or event.

stimulus.title: Document 7 · Wollstonecraft on reason and the rights of women
stimulus.content: “. . . if she be not prepared by education to become the companion of man, she will stop the progress of knowledge. . . . If women are to be excluded . . . prove first . . . that they want [lack] reason, else this flaw in your NEW CONSTITUTION will ever show that man must . . . act like a tyrant. . . .”
stimulus.citation: Source: Mary Wollstonecraft, A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, 1792 (adapted). Addressed to Talleyrand-Périgord, a member of the French National Assembly.
